Frontmatter defaults apply to query scoping and layout selection during the render; when the `<page>` tag and frontmatter both set a key, the tag wins.

Page gates apply in both spellings: frontmatter `require:` and `role:` gate the route exactly like the `<page require=... role=...>` tag. `auth=` other than an explicit opt-out (`none`, `public`, `false`) requires sign-in; an unknown value logs a warning. A `require=` with no valid `field:value` part answers 403 instead of admitting everyone. A page's `role=` (comma-separated, any-of) counts roles the account holds GLOBALLY: the `_benmore_users.role` column or an unexpired `_benmore_user_roles` grant with no group_id, each matched through the built-in hierarchy (admin > manager > editor > user) or, for a custom role, by name. An admin by global grant therefore opens `role="admin"` pages like an admin by column. A tenant membership role (groups.role_field) or a grant scoped to one group never opens a page: a page has no tenant to bound it, so gate tenant-role UI on data the API scopes, not on `role=`. GET /pdf/<page> applies the same rule, including any-of.

Pages are for browser sign-ins. A scoped credential (an API token or Bearer session issued with explicit scopes; '' and '*' are unscoped) never opens a page that has an `auth`, `role` or `require` gate: the route and GET /pdf/<page> answer 403 `{"error":"scoped_credential_page", "message": ..., "docs":"auth.credential_limits"}` before the gates, the `<query>` tags, the gotmpl queries or the typed sources run, whatever its scopes name. A page with no gate renders for it as for a signed-out visitor: no `user` values, `current_user` false, and queries and sources that see nobody. An unscoped token and a browser session pass `auth`, `role` and `require` as their account, and the page's `<query>` tags and gotmpl queries return what that account may read; GET /pdf/<page> renders the same page the same way. Encrypted-field masks, hidden columns and the read audit apply as for any viewer. An integration reads data through the generated API its scopes name: api({at:'auth'}) credential_limits.

Owner-scoped page queries (`<query scope="owner">`, shorthand `owned=`, gotmpl frontmatter `scope: owner`) wrap the page's WHERE in parentheses before adding the owner filter, return no rows when no one is signed in, and fail the page for shapes they can't scope (UNION; a 500, see query_tags). Template values in `where=` and in raw `<query sql>` bind as `?` arguments by position, never as SQL text; shorthand `pick=`/`owned=`/`from=` must name real columns.

`<query cache=>` results are cached per app and per viewer unmask class (query_tags), and sitemap.xml, llms.txt and feed.xml list only public pages (no auth/require/role/type/redirect/noindex pages, and no page with path parameters, see ssr_path_params). The generated sitemap lists only server-rendered pages, so a TSX/static site should ship `static/sitemap.xml`: an app's own `static/sitemap.xml` and `static/robots.txt` are served verbatim at /sitemap.xml and /robots.txt, like `static/llms.txt`. Absolute links in the generated files use `seo.url`, else the configured public origin (BENMORE_PUBLIC_URL / CORS_ORIGIN), else, on a hosted app, the request's host (a self-hosted app with neither set gets `http://localhost:<port>`: set `seo.url`). A hosted dev instance sends `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` and its generated robots.txt has no Sitemap line; see api(at:"environments") `dev_noindex`.
